summary.text: Sam Altman is an American technology executive and investor. He became president of Y Combinator around 2014 and stepped down in March 2019 to focus on OpenAI, which he co-founded and leads as CEO. He provided the entire $180 million first round of longevity startup Retro Biosciences and has invested more than $375 million in fusion company Helion. In 2019 he co-founded Tools for Humanity, the company behind the Worldcoin iris-scanning project, and he chaired nuclear startup Oklo until April 2025.

facts.claim: In 2019, Altman co-founded Tools for Humanity, which runs the Worldcoin project and verifies people by scanning their irises. Regulators have halted its operations in several places: Kenya suspended it in August 2023, Spain's data protection agency ordered it to stop collecting iris data in March 2024, Portugal's regulator imposed a 90-day suspension in March 2024, and Hong Kong's privacy commissioner ordered it to cease operations in May 2024.

facts.claim: Altman provided the entire $180 million first funding round of longevity startup Retro Biosciences, MIT Technology Review reported in 2023. He has also put more than $375 million into fusion company Helion.

connections.claim: Musk, an OpenAI co-founder, sued Altman and OpenAI in 2024, alleging they abandoned OpenAI's founding nonprofit mission. In May 2026, after a three-week trial, a federal judge in Oakland adopted an advisory jury's finding that Musk had filed too late and dismissed his claims. Musk said he would appeal.
